note: Corrected per the lead follow-up review's S2 finding: M4-C-boundary-targets-2026-09-09.json described a small, deliberately safe strip inside the visible wall, not the wall's actual boundary - pixels outside that strip were neither positive nor negative, but the old scorer counted all of them as false-positive area against any candidate that covered them. This version annotates the full visible wall each frame actually shows (re-inspected at source resolution via cropped zooms, not the resized preview), with three explicit categories: `positive_polygon` (confidently this wall's own material), `negative_polygons` (confidently NOT this wall - a different wall, the floor, a foreground occluder, an opening/gap) and `uncertain_polygons` (genuinely ambiguous transitions - the wall/back-wall corner, the wall/roof-gap junction - excluded from scoring entirely rather than guessed either way, per the review's 'record uncertainty as unknown, not negative'). Corners are still hand-estimated from static crops, not pixel-exact. Frozen with a content hash before scoring; scripts/boundary_pilot_c2.py refuses to run if this file changes afterward. The proposal path never reads this file.
